title: One father, all his children
hookLine: ek pitaa ekas ke ham baarik: one Father, and we are all His children (Sorath M5, ang 611)

cards: Siblings are complicated. They borrow your clothes without asking. They know exactly which button to push.
They tell your secrets at Thanksgiving. And yet, let anyone outside the family say a word against them, and something fierce can wake up. Siblings don't choose each other.
They're handed to each other by having the same parents. Guru Arjan took that simple fact and stretched it, in one line of Raag Sorath, across every human being alive.

teach.b: The line is on ang 611: ek pitaa ekas ke ham baarik, tu meraa gur haaee. One Father; we are children of the One. You are my Guru.
Ek is one. Pitaa, father, the same word we met in You are my father.

Baarik, children, little ones. And it goes on, in effect: listen, my friend, my soul is a sacrifice to you; show me a glimpse of the Lord. Four days ago Guru Arjan called the One father, mother, kin and brother.

That was vertical: me and the One. This line turns sideways. If there is one Father, everyone else is a brother or a sister, and you don't get to choose them, any more than you chose the ones at your own family table.

Notice he doesn't say we're all alike, or that we all agree, or that we'll all get along. Real siblings don't. The hymn makes a smaller and harder claim: we belong to each other, because we belong to the same One.
Nobody applies to be a sibling. Nobody earns a seat at the family table, and nobody can be voted off it.
The line has no membership test: the person you like least is as much a child of the One as the person you admire most. Then the hymn turns to friendship.

teach.h: A FRIEND WHO HELPS ME SEE THE ONE.
teach.b: Guru Arjan speaks to a friend, meetaa, and asks for help to see the One.
In the hymn, the others aren't only people to be kind to. They can be the ones who help a person find the Father.

how: Sikhs sing Guru Arjan's Sorath shabad with 'ek pitaa ekas ke ham baarik' in kirtan, and the line is quoted for the kinship of all people.

o: a father figure who leads the sangat
the eldest brother of the household
one Father, so everyone is a sibling

s: the line says all people are alike
it says we belong to each other, because we belong to the same One.
the line comes from Guru Arjan, in Raag Sorath
the hymn asks a friend to help the singer see the One
listen, my friend: show me a glimpse of the Lord.

games.q: if there's one Father, what are the people around you?
o: strangers who happen to be nearby.
games.why: one Father, all His children: you don't choose your siblings, but you belong to them.

practice: Bring to mind someone very different from you, in politics, faith or age, someone you find a little hard, and see their face.
Hold Guru Arjan's line over the two of you, one Father, and we are children of the One, and without forcing a warm feeling, just try on the word sibling and notice what resists and what softens.
If you pray, you can say Waheguru for both of you at once.

wordCard.voice: One father. Ek pitaa ekas ke ham baarik: one Father, and we are all children of the One, and in the hymn, every stranger is a sibling.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: children, little ones; ham baarik, we are the children.

carryVoice: Your line: all his children. No membership test, and nobody voted off. Six hundred fifty-seven days in.

sources.ref: Sorath M5, Ang 611 (ek pitaa ekas ke ham baarik)
